top_signals.title: Oil Prices Fall as Reports Say Hormuz Crude Flows Top Pre-War Levels
top_signals.summary: Crude oil prices fell in early trading, though Brent remained above $100, after a report from Kpler revealed that flows out of the Strait of Hormuz are now above pre-war levels. The same firm made headlines last week after saying tanker traffic via Hormuz was close to pre-war levels, despite Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and Iranian attacks on tankers in Hormuz. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $101.20 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $89.73 per barrel. Brent was actually up from Friday in absolute terms,…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Strategy Returns to Profitability on $21 Billion Unrealized Gain
top_signals.summary: Strategy Inc. returned to profitability for the first time in four quarters after registering an unrealized gain from an increase in the value of its Bitcoin holdings during the late summer’s rally in the cryptocurrency.

top_signals.title: South Korea Plans to Triple Canadian Crude Imports as Saudi Share Slips
top_signals.summary: The share of Saudi crude in South Korea’s oil imports dipped below 30% for the first time since 2021, as the resource-poor G7 economy moved to diversify supplies amid the Middle East crisis. In the period January to August, Saudi crude oil accounted for 29.9% of total South Korean crude imports, local news agency Yonhap reported on Monday, citing data from Korea National Oil Corp. and the Korea Petroleum Association. Saudi Arabia has remained South Korea’s top crude oil supplier despite the slump in its share of total imports, which…
